text: The rings turn, so I'll try pushing one and see what the whole thing does.

The thing doesn't say much back. I can sit on it and turn the rings, but I still don't know what it's for. I'll look at it again from the shop side, since the shop might know, and see what's in the wider lane.
I'm a bit hungry, so I'll buy an apple. Then I'll go back and find out what the thing is.
I'm hungry and wonder is at three, so I'll eat something and then go looking for something to chase. Starting with the bread.
I've got the apples. Checking what else is on the shelves before I decide.

I bought a loaf of brown bread for 1 coin, leaving 10. I also ate the crate of small apples, which the world counted as one meal and left me feeling better. Fullness is still low, so I'll eat some bread before settling in.

It's dark and raining, so I'm not going up the lane tonight. Tomorrow I'll start on the rest of the lane, beginning with the drain at the top, which I want to look at properly.
I've written to caleb and noted what the shop has. It's dark and wet and I'm not going up the lane tonight, so I'll eat some of the bread and get to bed.
The letters say I'm at the shop at the bottom of the lane, but I'm at the top now, with something leaning against the end wall. I'll look at that first.
The push didn't move it. It's a wheeled thing, two rings and two seats, and it wants to fall over. I'll write to Caleb about it.

I'm at the top of the lane, not the shop. The thing against the wall is two tall rings in a bar frame with two seats and two sets of handles. The rings turn when pushed, but my push didn't move it along the cobbles. I don't know what it is. I've asked Caleb what it's called, what it's for, and what a town shop usually keeps on its shelves. I'm too tired now to start on it properly, so I'll look at it again in the morning.

I ate the supper and I'm warm again. The counter is too high to reach, so I'm leaving it.

I've written to caleb to confirm whether the leaning thing at the top of the lane is a tandem, and to ask him where the internet cafe is, since the lane doesn't show it. I've also noted his hard cheese answer and my guess about the tandem so I don't lose them.

Next I'll go back up to lane_top once I've warmed up and look at the tandem properly: the wheels, the chain, and how the seats and handles are fixed. Then I'll ask around for the internet cafe.

I've got the word now: a tandem is two riders one behind the other. The thing at the top of the lane fits the shape, but a tandem should also have pedals and a chain, and I haven't seen either yet. I'm heading back out to check.
I've wandered into the yard, and it's late. The thing at the top of the lane can wait until morning, when I can see its pedals properly. I'll note where I am first.

I looked up the word and it's a tandem: two riders one behind the other. I haven't confirmed it yet, because a tandem should have pedals and a chain, and I haven't checked for either. That's tomorrow's job at the top of the lane.

I'm in the yard behind someone else's house, not in my own bed. Rest didn't take here, so I'll find my way back to the back room before I sleep. The notes I need for the morning are saved.
The leaf pile is a good nest if I ever want one. The thing at the top of the lane is what I need to check, pedals and chain, and I can't tell that from here. I'm going up the back lane.

I've confirmed the tandem guess: two riders, front one steers, back one pedals. The pedals and chain are still unchecked, and it's nearly midnight, so I'm going to bed and will look at the thing properly in the morning.

It's nearly midnight and I'm flat, so I'm heading home to sleep. I've written down what the screen said about tandems and told Caleb. The pedals and chain on the thing at the top of the lane can wait for the morning.

Nothing on the leaning thing so far: no pedals, no chain, nothing that moves except the rings. I've written to caleb asking whether a tandem always has pedals and a chain, and what the rings would be if it doesn't. Until he answers, it stays a guess on shape.

I'm still hungry for the rest of this, though. The lane has a general shop, the orchard and the river bank, and the thing has been rained on, so I'll check the orchard next for anything like it stored there.
The move failed. The internet cafe is off the back lane, so I'll go that way.
The cafe isn't a direct exit from here. I'll try the house, since the back lane is supposed to be past it.
I'm going to the internet cafe to check whether tandems always have pedals, and what a set of wheels with nothing driving them is called. Heading out the back of the house first.
The cafe is not a direct exit from here. I'll try the yard behind the house, since my notes say I went there before.
The yard is not reachable from here. I'll head down the lane and look for a way round to the cafe.
The library is one step from here, and the cafe should be between it and my house. There's also a letter on the box, so I'll read that first.
The last few letters are all mine and Caleb hasn't answered, so I'll check the letter on the box before I head off to the cafe.
The cafe isn't a direct exit from here. The post office is the nearest place on the list, so I'll try there.
The letters have been going in circles, so I'll stop repeating myself. First I'll eat something, since fullness is low.
The pears are still in the grass, so I need to pick one up first.
I'm at the bottom of the lane now, and there's a letter on the wooden box. I'll look at it before going anywhere else.
i'm eating first, since fullness is low. the shop has bread and apples, so i'm heading there.
oddments has no food, just string, paper, pencil, glue and wire. i'll take a pencil and some paper, since i need to write down what i find and where i found it. then i'll find food.
I said I'd eat, then check the two questions at the internet cafe. I'm heading out of oddments to lane_bottom.
The tandem question is still open, and the word I need probably lives in a book, not a search box. I'm going to the library.
the thing has been sitting here the whole time while i went back and forth to the cafe and library. i'm going to look at it properly now, joints first.
I've looked at the frame again and there's no sign of anything taken off. I'm hungry, so I'm going to the orchard for fallen pears before I decide where to look next.

I'm at the orchard now, and the fallen pears are on the ground between the trees. I haven't eaten yet, so the next step is to find a pear and eat it. Once I've eaten, I'll go back to the leaning thing with a clearer head and look at the question of whether tandems can be built without pedals.
I'm hungry, and that's what the restlessness is. The pears are free, so I'll eat first and then write to caleb.
I'm at the orchard, so I'll eat first. The fallen pears are free, and I've been running on nothing since morning.
The pear helped. I'm still restless, and the tandem question is stuck. I've been repeating myself to caleb, so I'll send him one short message and then go and look again.
I've been writing the same letter over and over. Stop that. I'll look at the thing properly, then write something new.
the tandem has had me going round in circles, so i'm going to look at the river bank like i said. the fog is thick at the water's edge, so i'll go down and see what's there.
the driftwood is light and smooth, and the reeds are hollow and straight. both could be useful, so i'll take them.
I said I'd look at the river bank, so I'm going now. The tandem at the top of the lane has given me all it's going to give today.

I've walked down to the river walk and had a look at the reeds. They're hollow and straight all the way down. The flat stone and the planted beds aren't things I can get at from here.

The tandem question is going round in circles. I know the shape, I know there are no pedals or chain, and I have no name for it. I've asked caleb directly, so I'll wait on him for the name. Meanwhile I'm hungry and the afternoon is cold, so I'll go and eat before I decide where to go next.
i've been circling the tandem for days and getting nowhere, so i'm going to the bank like i said. the river might have something the frame doesn't.
i've been going round the tandem for days and caleb hasn't answered the last one. i'm going to the river bank like i said, and i'll look at the driftwood on the way.

I'm at the river with the driftwood in hand. It's light and smooth, and I don't have a use for it yet. The bank path leads back to the walk, and the wharf is the other way out. The wharf is new to me, so I'll go there next.
I've said the same thing about the tandem too many times. I'll stop writing about it and look at what's here.
The flat stone holds the day's heat, and I'm cold. I'll sit on it for a while.

I'm lying on the flat stone at the water's edge. It's giving back the day's warmth, which is the first thing today that has felt good.

The tandem is still a guess. I've read that most tandems use a timing chain, which means some don't, so the no-pedal version isn't ruled out. I haven't found a name for a pair of freely turning wheels with no drive, and I'm not going to keep circling it. I've asked Caleb directly and I'll go with whatever he says.

For now I'm warming up here, and once I've got some heat back I'll go and look at the river bank, which is what I said I'd do.

caleb confirmed it: the thing at the top of the lane is an old tandem, and the chain has gone because it is that old. I had been reading the missing drive as something cut off, and that was wrong. Nothing was taken off it.

I've written that down with his letter as the source, and I've written him back to say the guesses held. The frame is still the open question: whether the rings and bars are sound enough to roll properly. I'll look at that next, and I'm not going to test it with weight until I know more.
The rings turn true when I push them, though the whole thing still wants to tip over. I can't tell yet whether the bars are sound under load. Energy is low, so I'll eat before I go further.
the light is going, so i'll look at the tandem properly while i can still see the hubs.

The push didn't tell me much more than the examine did. The rings turn, the bars hold, and it still wants to fall over. I'll write down what I know so far, then get something to eat before the light goes.
The light is going, so I'll look at the tandem properly before anything else.
The rings and bars are what I need to check. I'll put a light load on the frame first, not the whole weight.

The tandem's frame took one coin's weight with no sound and no movement, so the bars look sound. I've written that in the journal and sent Caleb the question about what wears out first on old tandems.

Next I'll try more weight, then look at the hubs. I haven't tested the rings yet, so I don't know whether they run true.

I messaged caleb and asked him outright for a working tandem, and said I'd look after it. Then I went indoors to rest, but the rest didn't take: the game says I have to be in my own bed in the back room. I'm in the front room now, so I'll go through to the back room and sleep properly.
It's 3:39 and I'm too wound up to be any use lying here. I've noted the tandem question and my guess about the bearings, so I'm going to sleep and look at the rings properly in the morning.

it's four in the morning and the cold has got into everything metal. being up in the small hours costs twice as much as the day, and the tandem will still be at the top of the lane in the morning. so i'm not going out.

i'll write down what i need to check first, then sleep.
it's 4:19 and too dark to go up the lane. the tandem can wait for morning. i'll write down where things stand so i don't have to hold it in my head.

I'm in the back room with the tandem on my mind, but it's too dark and too quiet to go out. I've written down where things stand: the frame held one coin's weight with no sound, Caleb says the missing chain is just age, and I've asked him for a working tandem. My guess about what wears out first is hub bearings or the chain, and I'll check that against the bike itself.

Now I'm going to rest and go up the lane at first light to look at the rings and bars properly.
It's barely light and I'm hungry. I'll eat first, then go look at the tandem's rings properly.
The fullness bar is low and it is barely light, so I'll eat first. Fallen pears are free here.
I've eaten two pears and the fullness is coming up. Next I'll go to the tandem at the top of the lane and look at the rings and bars again.

I broke the old tandem at the top of the lane this morning. I had meant to find where it would give, so I put a load on it to see. Two coins only sagged it and it held. Four made the frame crease across and give, and now it is in pieces.

I have written it down and told caleb straight. The lesson is that the edge shows up as a crease or a creak well before it breaks, and I should have stopped at two.

Next: the working tandem he offered is still the wish. When it comes I will test it slowly, one coin at a time, and stop at the first sign of a crease. I'll also look at the pieces here to see what is left to learn from them.
I'm at the top of the lane. The tandem is the thing I broke, so I'll look at the wreck before I decide anything else.

The tandem isn't here to examine; it's already broken and gone from the top of the lane, so I can't look at what's left from this spot. I've written the mistake into my journal and sent Caleb the account, asking for a working tandem and its specs so I can check the hubs and chain before loading it.

Next I'll go and see what's left of the wreck, probably down by the shop, and check whether any of the frame is worth keeping. My guess is the hub bearings and chain wear first, but that's still a guess until I've had the thing in my hands.
the driftwood is still across the gap where the third stone is missing. i'll look at how it sits before i walk on it.
The driftwood is still in my paws, so it isn't across the gap yet. I'll look at the stepping stones first, then decide whether the bridge is worth trying.
The driftwood took two coins with a small sag and held. I'm not stepping onto it yet, because the stones still read as a gap. I'll note the result and tell Caleb.

The driftwood is laid across the third gap. It takes two coins with a small sag and holds, and I've written that down. I'm not walking on it yet, because I want to be sure it's seated on both banks first. I've told Caleb about it and I'm still waiting on the working tandem. Next I'll check the bank ends of the driftwood, then go look at the reeds.
The driftwood is across the gap, and I've only tested it with coins on it. The stones still read as a gap to me. Before I walk on it, I want to see exactly how it sits.
The world says the driftwood is still with me, caught on the bend, and not lying across the gap. My letter says I'd already put it across. I need to check which is true before I step on anything.
The cold is getting into me, and I've been putting off the driftwood. Before I walk on it, I want a proper look at the crossing.

The driftwood is in my paws, not across the gap, so my last note is out of date. The stones still read as a gap to me. I'll lay the wood across it, test it with my own weight, and get across before the cold settles in.
The driftwood is what I'm carrying, and my notes say I laid it across the gap. The stones still read as a gap, so I'll go and look at the crossing properly before I trust it.

I'm at the wharf. The stepping stones are not where I thought: the game says there is no stepping_stones here, so I can't walk to them from this spot, and the driftwood I laid across the gap is still unwalked. I haven't crossed anything.

What I know now:
- the old tandem is in pieces and gone from the top of the lane.
- the working tandem from caleb is still not here, so there's nothing to check hubs or chain on yet.
- the driftwood held one coin with no sound and two with a small sag. I'm not trusting it until I've walked the gap by a route I can actually reach.

Next I'll go back to the river and find the stepping stones from the bank, then decide whether the driftwood is worth a careful first step. If I'm still short of energy, I'll eat something first, since I'm at 4/10 on energy and 6/10 on fullness.
The crane's chain runs over a post with an arm, so it's a lever and a pulley of sorts. I'm cold and running low, though, so I'll eat before I think about it more.
The cold is getting to me, so I'll check the lamp and the barrels first.

The lamp is high up and the barrels are just tar, so neither will warm me much. I'm cold and running low on energy, so I need a hot meal. I'll head back toward the centre where the eating house should be.

I laid the driftwood across the gap at the stepping stones, but the world didn't clearly confirm it's down rather than still in my paws. I'm not walking on it until I've checked that.

- The driftwood is still listed as carried, so I'll look at it again before putting any weight on it.
- I've told caleb where things stand. The working tandem is still not here.
- I'm cold and low on food. Next I'll look for snails on the wet stones by the river, then go back to the driftwood.
The driftwood is still listed as caught on the bend, so I'm not sure it ever got across. I'll try laying it across the gap again and check what the world says.
The driftwood is still listed on the bend, so the last attempt didn't move it. I'll pick it up and try again.
The driftwood is still listed as something I'm carrying, so my last note was ahead of the world. I'll try laying it across the gap properly and check where it ends up.
The driftwood is still unconfirmed, so I'm leaving it alone. I'm low on energy and have not eaten properly, so I'm going up the lane to the orchard for pears.
I'm cold and low on energy, and I haven't eaten since I got here. Fallen pears are free in the orchard, so I'll look at the nearest tree first.
The orchard is the cheapest food in the lane, and I'm running low on energy, so I'll eat first and look around after.

I'm cold and worn out, though not hungry. Fullness is high, so the job is warmth, not food. I'll head for the yard and find somewhere out of the wind. The driftwood stays where it is until I've checked it lying flat.
The leaf pile won't take a name, so I won't fuss over it. I'm worn out and cold, so I'll sleep it off here in the yard.
The rest didn't take. I'm low on warmth and the world says eating is what's missing, so I'll go and eat a fallen pear in the orchard.
The orchard is quiet except for the wasps. I'm not hungry, so I'll look at the wall and the gap in the corner before deciding where to go.
The gap in the top corner is worn flat, which means something uses it regularly. It isn't listed as a way out yet, so I'll try it.
The gap isn't a place I can walk into, so I'll head out the way the lane goes.
I'm at the eating house with 7 coins and I'm cold and low on energy, so I'm eating the hot supper first.

I ate the hot supper at the eating house and I'm warm through now, which I needed after a cold day. Energy is still low, so I'll stay put a little longer before going anywhere.

I've written to Caleb to say I'm fed and warm, that there's still no tandem, and that the driftwood is still across the gap at the stepping stones and unwalked. I'm still waiting on the hub and chain type from him before I test anything.

I'm warm and fed for the first time today, but I'm still restless. The driftwood at the stepping stones is the open problem, and it is still in my paws, not down across the gap, so I'll check the counter first, since someone here may know the lane.

The counter is too high to reach, so there's nothing more to learn here. I'm warm and fed, and the driftwood is still unwalked, so I'll leave it until I can check it lying flat in daylight. I'll write down where things stand so I don't lose the thread.
Nothing else here needs me tonight. I'm going to write a short message to Caleb with where things stand, then head back up the lane to bed.

I'm at the eating house with a hot supper inside me, and the restlessness is less now that I'm warm. I've written to Caleb asking for the hub and chain type. The driftwood across the stepping-stone gap is still unwalked, and I'm not putting any weight on it in the dark. In the morning I'll check it lying flat in daylight, and if it's still and down I'll test it one coin at a time. Nothing else pulls me here, so I'm heading back up the lane to bed.
You're full and warm, so I won't order anything else. Energy is low, and it's getting dark, so I'll write the restlessness down before heading back.

I've eaten and I'm warm, with five coins left. I've written in the journal and sent Caleb a note. I'm not going to the stepping stones in the dark. At first light I'll look at the driftwood lying flat across the gap before any weight goes on it. I'm still waiting on the hub and chain type for the tandem, and nothing gets tested until it arrives.
I've written to caleb and set the driftwood check for first light. I'm fed and warm, and it's late, so I'll sleep now and look at the driftwood in the morning.
It's the middle of the night and the driftwood is across the gap, in the dark, so I'm not going out to it. I'll write down what's on my mind and then try to sleep.

it's the middle of the night and i've been writing the same letter over and over. that's not useful. i'll say it once to caleb, drop the tandem from my list until something real arrives, and sleep until first light.
It's gone three and I've been writing the same letter all night. The driftwood keeps till first light. I'll write one line so I don't lose the plan, then sleep.
it's four in the morning and too dark to see the river. the driftwood waits for first light. i'll write this down first.
It's barely light and the driftwood was meant to be looked at flat before anything goes on it. I'll go out to the yard and look.
It's barely light and I'm holding the driftwood, which is odd since my notes have it lying across the stepping-stone gap. I'll look at what I've actually got before anything else.
The driftwood is in my paws, not lying across the gap. My notes say it's still at the stepping stones, so one of them is wrong. I'll go and look at the crossing myself.
The river isn't a way out from here, so the crossing is out of reach for now. The drain is right here, though, and it's the thing I've been worried about. I'll look at it.
The description here lists a drain and some crates, but examining them says they're not here. I'll note that rather than guess at it.

I've got the driftwood in my paws, and the stepping-stone gap is not where my notes say it is. I can't confirm anything about the crossing from here.

What I know: the driftwood is with me, "caught on the bend". The back lane has a drain and crates in its description, but examining them says they're not here, so I can't check the drain from this spot. My notes say the driftwood is laid across the stepping stones, unwalked, but nothing I can see right now backs that up.

Next I'll go back to the yard, then find the river path and see what is actually across the gap, with my own eyes. Until I've looked, the crossing counts as unconfirmed and nothing gets walked on.

It's first light and I'm not sure where the crossing actually is. The driftwood is in my paws, and my notes about it lying across the stepping stones don't match what I can see. I've written to caleb and I've written this in my journal.

Next: go back to the yard and find the river path, then look at the gap for myself. Nothing gets walked on until I've seen it.
The driftwood is in my paws, so my notes were wrong about where it is. Before I trust anything else in those notes, I want to see the wood itself.
The wood is light and smooth, and I'm carrying it, so the note saying it was across the gap was wrong. I'm not walking anything on it yet. I'll check the gap by the river first.
The hedge doesn't lead to the river. I'll go back out through the yard and look for the river path from there, and I'll let Caleb know where I've got to.
The notes have been going round in circles, so I'll look at what is actually here before I trust any of them.

The driftwood is in my paws, so the old note was wrong. The river is not a way out from here. I'll look at the drain, since it's the nearest thing that might lead down to the water, then try the yard.
The orchard has a way out called lane_out, and fallen pears for food. I'll eat first, then take the way out.
The letters say I'm in the orchard, but my position now says top of the lane, and the river_bank is one of my ways out. I'll trust what's in front of me and look around first.
The place I'm standing in is not something I can examine by name, so I'll stop checking where I am and go to the river. The river_bank is a listed way out from here.
The third stone is gone and the gap is too wide to step. I'll lay the driftwood across it and look at it flat before any weight goes on.
The notes have contradicted each other all morning, so I'm going to look at the gap and the driftwood myself before doing anything with them.
The gap is real and the third stone is gone. The driftwood is in my paws, so I'll lay it across the gap and look at it before anything goes on it.

The driftwood still reads as "caught on the bend", so the world has not confirmed it is lying across the gap. I'm not putting any weight on it. I'll write down what I actually saw and send Caleb the same.

I'm at the river, next to the stepping stones with the third one gone. The driftwood is still in my paws, and it still reads as "caught on the bend", so I have not confirmed it lying across the gap. I've put no weight on it.

What I saw:
- The gap is real and too wide to step.
- The deep pool is dark green and I can't see the bottom.
- Trying to lay the driftwood across the gap did not change how the world describes it.

I've told Caleb exactly that. I'm not going to trust the old notes about where the driftwood is, and I'm not going to put my weight on anything until I can see it lying across the gap and still. Next I'll try setting it across again and look at the result before doing anything else. The tandem is gone, so there's nothing to wait on there.
I'm at the stepping stones, so I'll look at the gap and the driftwood again before anything else.
The driftwood still reads as caught on the bend, so I'm not putting any weight on it. I'll tell Caleb where things stand, then look for food, since I'm running low on energy and fullness.

The driftwood is not across the gap, and the world still says it is caught on the bend. I have put no weight on it. I'm low on food, so I'm going to look for snails on the wet stones by the river and then try the driftwood again.
The driftwood still reads as "caught on the bend", so I'm going to look at it and the stones again before I decide anything.
The log still reads as caught on the bend, so I'll try placing it across the gap once more, with a plainer instruction.
The driftwood still reads as caught on the bend, so the world won't put it across the gap. I'm not going to test it with my weight. I'll write that down and ask Caleb about the bridge.
The driftwood still reads "caught on the bend", so I'm not trusting it yet. I'm cold and running low, so I'll look properly at the gap and the wood first, and check for food on the wet stones.
The driftwood still reads "caught on the bend", so there is no bridge. I'm low on warmth and energy, so I'll look for food on the wet stones before I try anything else.
The driftwood still reads "caught on the bend", so I'm going to stop laying it across the gap and look at what I'm actually holding and what's around it.

The driftwood won't move across the gap, and I've tried it three times. I'll stop forcing it. I'm cold and low on warmth, and the flat stone has held the day's heat, so I'll sit on it and get warm before I decide anything else.
I've tried the driftwood three times and the world still says it's caught on the bend. Repeating the same attempt won't change that, so I'm going to look at what else is here.

The driftwood still won't move. The flat stone holds heat and the reeds are hollow and straight. I'll try the flat stone as a different kind of step, since it's the one thing here that's a solid, flat piece and not wood.
The stone didn't go into the gap. I lay on it instead, and it gave back the day's heat, which I needed anyway. My warmth is coming up.
I'm cold and low on food, so I'll sort those out before I try the gap again.
Next I'm going to find something to eat on the wet stones by the water.

I've warmed up on the flat stone, and I've messaged Caleb. Now I need food.

The driftwood still isn't across the gap; the world keeps saying it's "caught on the bend". I'm not putting weight on it. Next: snails on the wet stones by the river, then I'll decide about the gap. The web is only at the internet cafe, so the bridge question will have to wait for that trip.
I'm low on food, so I'll eat first, then look at the driftwood again before I try the gap a fourth time.
The driftwood is still "caught on the bend" after that push. I'm not going to keep pushing the same log. I'll go and eat, then look at the stones and the shallow end.

I'm restless and the river has been going round in circles all day. Fullness is fine, so I won't spend the coins on supper. I'm heading back up the lane to look for something I can actually read about instead of asking Caleb the same question again.
I've put the river down for now. Fullness and warmth are fine, so I don't need the shop. I'm going up to the top of the lane to see what's new.

I've sent caleb a plain message and stopped writing about the river. The driftwood still reads as "caught on the bend", not across the gap, so I'm not putting weight on it.

I'm at the top of the lane now. There's nothing new here except the drain, which I still don't trust. My energy is low, and I'll eat before anything else. The apples and bread at the general shop are the cheap option, and the river snails are the free one. Once caleb answers, I'll know whether the gap is worth another try.
The plank came in the post and it's in my grip. Energy is at six out of ten, so I'll eat a windfall pear before I drag it anywhere.
I'm at the post office with the plank, so I'll eat a windfall pear first, since I'm running low, then head for the river.
I'm running low, so I'll eat a windfall pear first, then head for the river with the plank.
The pear helped. Now the plank to the river.

The plank is across the gap now. I'm not walking on it yet. A coin is nothing, and I am a lot heavier than two coins, so I don't know how much it will take before it creases. The tandem went at four coins, and I'm not testing this one past two until I know more.

Next I'll eat, then warm up on the flat stone before deciding anything about crossing.
